facts.text: Rector was originally called Mechanicsburg in the 19th century but was renamed in the early 20th century to honor a prominent local family.
The Powdermill Nature Reserve, founded in 1956 by the Carnegie Museum of Natural History, covers over 2,200 acres south of Rector.
Rector sits in the Laurel Highlands, about 55 miles southeast of Pittsburgh, at an elevation of roughly 1,299 feet.
The community lies just 3 miles south of Ligonier and 17 miles southeast of Greensburg, placing it within easy reach of regional highways.
Indigenous Lenape people once used the Ligonier Valley trails for migration and hunting before European settlement.
The valley’s climate averages 50°F yearly, with July highs around 83°F and January lows near 18°F, and receives about 45 inches of snow annually.
